To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have discovered a new class of radio galaxies that have a cool core and a shock front in the intracluster medium; (2) these radio galaxies are the only ones known to have both a shock front and a cool core, and they are the only known radio galaxies to have a shock front that is associated with the inflation of the lobes rather than a merger; (3) the shocks in these galaxies are likely to be the result of a single, powerful outburst; (
(1) the radio lobes of 3C 286 have inflated to a radius of 0.5 M pc, and (2) the energy of the radio outburst is roughly 30% the thermal energy of gas within the radius.

we have detected multiple surface brightness discontinuity features in the X-ray gas of 3C 286 that are consistent with shocks produced by the inflation of a nuclear outburst, which is the first time such a phenomenon has been detected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the physical processes that occur when a galaxy’s supermassive black hole is actively feeding, i.e., accreting matter from its surrounding environment.
the study of the physics of the hot intergalactic medium (IGM).
the study of the physics of the intracluster medium, and in particular with the effects of active galactic nuclei (AGN) on the evolution of the hot intracluster medium (ICM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
3C288 is a galaxy in a poor cluster with a central temperature of ∼3 kev and a cool core that has been recently heated and disturbed by a nuclear outburst that has inflated the radio lobes.
the nuclear activity in 3C 286 was triggered by a merger event.
a nuclear outburst in 3C 28 has recently reheated the cool core of a 3 keV cluster, which is in transition between a cooling core and a non-cooling core.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy deposited into the ICM by the nuclear outflow was sufficient to heat the gas to the observed temperature, and that the gas has been reheated on the cooling time scale of ∼10 7 yr, thus preventing the gas from cooling.
the energy deposited in the cluster gas by the radio source outburst is comparable to the thermal energy of gas within the radius where shocks are detected.
the energy deposited into the ICM by the outburst has not yet had time to cool.
